output.title: Geopolitical and Regulatory Risks
output.description: Vestas faces significant risks from shifting geopolitical tensions and regulatory changes, including conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, trade tensions, tariffs, sanctions, export controls, and industrial policies that alter the regulatory landscape. These developments can disrupt and delay supply chains, increase costs, weaken project economics, reduce market volumes, and challenge cost efficiency and competitiveness.

output.title: Project Execution Risk
output.description: Project execution at Vestas involves delivering complex onshore and offshore projects within specified parameters relating to quality, cost, and timeline. Execution is affected by delays in production capacity ramp‑up, quality control issues during scaling, and supply chain disruptions, which can lead to delays, cost overruns, and margin erosion. The lack of industry‑wide standardisation and insufficient logistical infrastructure further complicate timely delivery, while external factors such as regulatory frameworks and geopolitical shifts also pose risks.

output.title: Cyber Attacks on Digital Assets
output.description: Vestas’ digital and other critical assets are exposed to cyber attacks. A cyber attack may disrupt energy production, cause electricity outages, and lead to significant economic loss and reputational damage.

output.title: Carbon taxes and tariffs
output.description: High carbon taxes and tariffs raise the price of greenhouse‑gas‑intensive materials such as steel. This increase in material costs raises the overall cost of producing wind turbines.

output.title: Injury‑Related Workforce Risk
output.description: Potential injuries to the company’s own workforce can cause delays, lost work hours, and compensation costs. These impacts pose a financial risk to the organization.

output.title: Injuries to Value‑Chain Workers
output.description: Potential injuries to value‑chain workers pose a risk. Such injuries could lead to delays, lost work hours and compensation costs.

output.title: Fines for child or forced labour
output.description: Vestas faces the risk of fines related to child and forced labour within its global supplier network. This risk arises from potential violations of labour laws and regulations governing the treatment of workers in the value chain, which could lead to legal penalties.

output.title: Insufficient market conditions
output.description: Inadequate grid expansion, ineffective auction design, and permit delays could increase costs, hinder investments, and reduce the viability of wind deployment. These conditions limit the ability to deploy wind projects effectively.

output.title: Cyber security risks
output.description: Cyber attacks might disrupt business operations, expose intellectual property, or cause legal liability. These impacts could impair the company’s ability to operate effectively and lead to potential legal consequences.

output.title: Risk of corruption and bribery
output.description: Vestas’ global presence presents an increased risk of exposure to corruption and bribery. This risk arises from operating in multiple jurisdictions where differing anti‑corruption laws and enforcement practices may apply, potentially leading to legal and reputational consequences.
